topicName: Probes (Liveness, Readiness, Startup) and Lifecycle Hooks
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Kubernetes Probes and Lifecycle Hooks"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensuring high availability and graceful operations in Kubernetes requires a deep understanding of container health checking and lifecycle management. This tutorial covers Probes (Liveness, Readiness, Startup) and Lifecycle Hooks (PostStart, PreStop)."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Startup Probes"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Startup probes are used to know when an application container has started. If such a probe is configured, it disables liveness and readiness checks until it succeeds, making sure that slow-starting containers do not get killed by liveness probes."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: startup-probe-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: slow-start-app
    image: my-app:1.0
    startupProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
      failureThreshold: 30
      periodSeconds: 10"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Liveness Probes"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Liveness probes determine when to restart a container. If the liveness probe fails, Kubernetes kills the container, and the Pod's restart policy dictates the next steps."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: liveness-probe-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-app:1.0
    livenessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /healthz
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 15
      periodSeconds: 20"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Readiness Probes"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Readiness probes determine whether a container is ready to accept traffic. If the readiness probe fails, the endpoints controller removes the Pod's IP address from the endpoints of all Services."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: readiness-probe-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-app:1.0
    readinessProbe:
      httpGet:
        path: /ready
        port: 8080
      initialDelaySeconds: 5
      periodSeconds: 10"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Container Lifecycle Hooks"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Lifecycle hooks expose events in the container management lifecycle and allow containers to be aware of events in their management lifecycle and execute code implemented in a handler when this lifecycle event occurs."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PostStart: This hook is executed immediately after a container is created. There is no guarantee that the hook will execute before the container entrypoint is mapped."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"PreStop: This hook is called immediately before a container is terminated due to an API request or management event such as a liveness probe failure."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: lifecycle-hooks-pod
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: my-app:1.0
    lifecycle:
      postStart:
        exec:
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "echo Hello from the postStart handler > /usr/share/message"]
      preStop:
        exec:
          command: ["/usr/sbin/nginx", "-s", "quit"]"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always define a Startup Probe for applications with long initialization phases."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Keep Liveness and Readiness probes distinct. Liveness checks if the app is broken, while Readiness checks if it can serve traffic."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use PreStop hooks to gracefully drain active connections before container termination."}]
